display.purpose: The decorative ITALIA composition; preserve source measurements and crop within its frame.

headline.purpose: Editorial page and room titles with Cyrillic-capable serif type.

heading-lg.purpose: The smaller gallery heading and notched showcase title.

title.purpose: The minimum serif title scale; smaller functional headings use Inter. Legal and admissions-changes titles use a local 34–52px clamp with wrapping for long Russian words.

heading.purpose: Inherited numeric emphasis; not a general sans-serif display role. The current price line uses local leading.

heading-sm.purpose: Compact section headings in working surfaces.

body-sm.purpose: Readable instructions and ordinary supporting prose.

label.purpose: Actions, captions, and small navigation labels.

micro.purpose: Approved notched-card inscription only; never essential task instructions.

shadows.name: flat
shadows.purpose: All surfaces and text remain without shadows. Focus is an outline.

motion.name: gallery-reveal
motion.purpose: Progressive heading entrances; immediate content under reduced motion.

motion.name: gallery-art
motion.purpose: Subtle circular painting movement and hexagon rotation.

motion.name: room-header
motion.purpose: Header reversal on entry into ink rooms.

narrative.overview:
iItaly presents the journey to studying in Italy as a sequence of calm gallery rooms. Putty walls, ink-black rooms, classical paintings, and monumental serif type create the atmosphere. Compact, readable utility type gives applicants a practical place to choose, understand, and complete their next step.

The system is restrained and flat. Art and typography carry its character; surfaces use tonal contrast, hairline boundaries, and deliberate space. Russian and Cyrillic support are essential. The previous warm SaaS identity, saturated accents, decorative assistant portraits, shadows, and gradients have been replaced.
keyCharacteristics: A fixed eight-color neutral palette with hard transitions between light and dark rooms.
Playfair Display for editorial moments; Inter for reading, controls, and data.
Public-domain Italian paintings in full-bleed panels and circular vignettes.
Compact pill actions, flat bone cards, notched showcases, and hexagonal indicators.
Motion that clarifies entrances and state while preserving reduced-motion access.

rules.name: The Contextual Contrast Rule
rules.body: Use ink for small secondary text on putty. Graphite is suitable on bone; vellum and paper are the corresponding text roles in ink rooms. The default `--text-secondary` and `--text-muted` aliases therefore resolve to ink on putty; graphite remains an explicit bone-surface choice. Do not assume a muted token is readable on every surface.

rules.name: The Eight Colors Rule
rules.body: New UI colors must resolve to the eight frontmatter primitives. Legacy names such as cream, crimson, cloud, warm, accent, and apple are compatibility aliases, not permission to restore old colors. Do not generate tonal ramps or introduce derived palette colors, including in documentation previews.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Playfair Display handles editorial headings at 34px and above. Inter handles utility text in the 9–26px range, with the inherited 43px numeric exception. Both families use only weights 400 and 500.

rules.name: The Legible Detail Rule
rules.body: Essential body and control text begins at 12px. The 9px inscription and small artwork credit are deliberate, localized exceptions; do not spread them to task instructions.

rules.name: The Flat Gallery Rule
rules.body: Express hierarchy through tone, type, spacing, and geometry. Do not introduce shadow or gradient tokens, including through legacy utilities.

dos: **Do** use the exact eight-color palette and choose secondary text by its surface.
**Do** pair Cyrillic-capable Playfair Display headings with Inter utility text at weights 400 and 500.
**Do** preserve the monumental wordmark, restrained pills, flat bone cards, and geometric showcase.
**Do** use locally served classical paintings with the source manifest and credits intact.
**Do** preserve visible keyboard focus, current-state semantics, readable task details, and reduced-motion behavior.
**Do** distinguish a labeled product example from an applicant's real plan or result.
donts: **Don't** reintroduce saturated interface accents, shadows, gradients, glass, or the former warm SaaS styling.
**Don't** use small serif copy, ornamental display type for controls, or unapproved display weights.
**Don't** apply the micro inscription size to essential instructions, controls, or legal copy.
**Don't** turn compatibility names or reference-brand examples into new visual requirements.
**Don't** use modern stock photography, generated assistant portraits, or 3D character decoration in gallery surfaces.
**Don't** duplicate navigation or let floating controls cover the primary task action.
